findings.evidence: UPDATE IGNORE pre-check always checks `newTableData`: `pkg/executor/update.go:212`, then calls `updateRecord(..., ignoreErr=true)`: `pkg/executor/update.go:222`. INSERT IGNORE ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE does the same with `newData`: `pkg/executor/insert.go:482` and `pkg/executor/insert.go:492`. But FK semantics for referred-FK (parent being updated) must check the *old* referenced key: `FKCheckExec.updateRowNeedToCheck` uses `oldRow` when `fkc.ReferredFK != nil`: `pkg/executor/foreign_key.go:168` and `pkg/executor/foreign_key.go:195`. Because `updateRecord` skips `updateRowNeedToCheck` entirely when `ignoreErr=true`: `pkg/executor/write.go:224`, referred-FK violations (1451) can be missed and the update applied. Integration outputs added/updated in this commit show no warning emitted for the parent-side 1451 cases (file ends immediately after the IGNORE statement): `tests/integrationtest/r/executor/update.result:905` and `tests/integrationtest/r/executor/insert.result:2144`. Checked later history: still not fixed on `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`), same missing warning lines at `upstream/master:tests/integrationtest/r/executor/update.result:905` and `upstream/master:tests/integrationtest/r/executor/insert.result:2147`.
findings.fix: When `IGNORE` is in effect, FK pre-check must distinguish FK types: for `FK != nil` (modify child), check `newRow`; for `ReferredFK != nil` (modify parent with RESTRICT/NO ACTION), check `oldRow` (the key currently referenced by children). Concretely, avoid calling `checkFKIgnoreErr` once on a single row for all `fkChecks`; instead run per-check with the correct row source (or change `checkFKIgnoreErr` to accept both `oldRow/newRow` and branch internally). Also avoid skipping the normal FK trigger pipeline for successful rows unless equivalent locking/checking is preserved.
findings.impact: Data consistency / SQL semantics: `UPDATE IGNORE` and `INSERT IGNORE ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` can silently apply parent key changes that should be rejected (1451) under RESTRICT/NO ACTION, potentially leaving orphan child rows and breaking foreign key invariants; also diverges from expected IGNORE behavior (should skip offending row and emit warning).
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed as of `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): unchanged behavior in integration outputs (`upstream/master:tests/integrationtest/r/executor/update.result:905`, `upstream/master:tests/integrationtest/r/executor/insert.result:2147`) and ignore-FK precheck remains `newData`-based (see `upstream/master:pkg/executor/write.go:250`).
findings.verify: Add/extend assertions for the existing integration cases: `tests/integrationtest/t/executor/update.test:697` and `tests/integrationtest/t/executor/insert.test:1610`. Verify that parent-side 1451 under IGNORE emits a warning and does not change the parent key (e.g., `select` after the IGNORE statement shows parent row unchanged and child still references an existing parent), and that child-side 1452 still becomes warning + skipped row. Minimal SQL repro: create parent/child with FK on `ref`, make a child reference `ref=2`, then run `update ignore parent set ref=3 where id=2` / `insert ignore into parent values (2,3) on duplicate key update ref=3` and ensure it warns 1451 and leaves `parent.ref` as 2.
findings.what: Referred-FK (parent-side) UPDATE/ON-DUP-UPDATE is checked against the wrong row image in IGNORE mode, so 1451 violations can be missed and applied (no warning), breaking FK integrity.

subject: executor: ignore foreign key error in `UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE ignore` (#56682)
summary: Found a Blocker: IGNORE-mode FK pre-check uses `newRow` for all FK checks, but referred-FK (parent update, 1451) must be checked on `oldRow`. Because IGNORE also skips the normal FK trigger checks, parent-side violations can be missed and applied with no warning; this remains unfixed on upstream/master.
